narrative: The model estimates a 55% probability that you will leave your job, which is slightly more likely than staying and is why the promotion was denied. This is a risk-based decision, not a certainty. The strongest signal was your total work experience: with 11 or more years overall, you differ from most employees predicted to stay, only about 15% of whom have that much experience, and this pushed the prediction toward leaving. The second most influential signal was that you reported no other job opportunities; that factor pushed toward staying and is a genuine retention strength. The third strongest signal, your 1 to 5 years in your current organization, also pushed toward leaving, even though it is common among employees predicted to stay. Overall, the no-other-opportunities factor was not enough to offset the leaving signals, so the model sees you as a modest flight risk. Next, the organization should discuss your career path and promotion criteria openly and check whether your experience is being used and rewarded. You should clarify what development, recognition, or role change would make staying worthwhile; if those needs are not addressed, the predicted risk may remain.
